title: Baseline Grids, Flow Columns & Frame Margins
subtitle: Vertical Rhythm, Multi-Column Text Threading & Justification

learningObjectives: Understand the typographic theory of vertical rhythm and the Document Baseline Grid.
Configure the Baseline Grid Manager (spacing, start position, display thresholds).
Set up multi-column text frames with gutters and link text flows across pages (text threading).
Diagnose and resolve overset text indicators, text frame margins, and vertical justification.
standardSections.foundationalKnowledge: In professional editorial design, nothing looks more amateur than facing pages where lines of text do not align horizontally across adjacent columns. When body copy drifts out of vertical alignment, the visual rhythm of the spread collapses. The solution is the Baseline Grid: an invisible horizontal metric ladder running across the entire document. When paragraphs are configured with 'Align to Baseline Grid', the baseline of every letterform automatically locks onto these grid rungs. This guarantees that whether a text frame has 1, 2, or 4 columns, every line of text across facing pages aligns with laser precision.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Configure the Document Baseline Grid
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Go to View > Baseline Grid Manager. Check the box labeled 'Use baseline grid'. Set 'Grid spacing' to match your intended body copy leading (e.g. 14 pt or 5 mm). Set 'Start position' to 'Top margin'. Check 'Show baseline grid' and set 'Display threshold' to 50% so grids remain visible when zoomed out.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Create a 3-Column Text Frame
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Select the Frame Text Tool (T). Click and drag a text frame spanning the margins of your left page. In the Context Toolbar, change 'Columns' from 1 to 3. Set 'Gutter' to 5mm. Notice the frame immediately divides into 3 equal editorial columns.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Align Paragraphs to Baseline Grid
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Insert placeholder text via Text > Insert Filler Text. Open the Paragraph Studio. Expand the 'Baseline Grid' section and check 'Align to baseline grid'. Notice all lines of text immediately snap into perfect vertical alignment across all 3 columns.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Thread Text Flow to the Next Page
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Draw another 3-column text frame on the right facing page. Return to the left frame. Notice a small blue triangle icon in the lower-right corner. Click this triangle (your cursor turns into a linking link icon), then click inside the right page's text frame. Text now flows seamlessly from page to page!

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Headlines breaking the baseline grid rhythm
commonPitfalls.cause: Setting a 28pt headline with 32pt leading on a 14pt baseline grid forces the following paragraph to skip awkward rungs.
commonPitfalls.solution: Always set headline leading to an exact integer multiple of your baseline grid (e.g. if the grid is 14pt, set headline leading to 28pt or 42pt).

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Overset text disappearing silently into the void
commonPitfalls.cause: A text frame is too small for its content; the overflow text is hidden without warning in print.
commonPitfalls.solution: Watch for the red eye icon in the lower right of the text frame. Affinity Publisher Preflight panel (Window > Preflight) will also flag 'Text frame overflow' as an error.

commonPitfalls.cause: Drawing text frames freely with snapping disabled.
commonPitfalls.solution: Turn on Snapping (; [Semicolon] alone; Ctrl+; toggles Guides) and ensure 'Snap to margins' is checked.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is the primary editorial purpose of aligning body text to a Document Baseline Grid?
options: It ensures that lines of text across multiple columns and facing pages sit on identical horizontal rungs, maintaining perfect vertical rhythm across the entire publication spread.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: A baseline grid enforces uniform vertical alignment across columns and spreads, preventing the distracting staggered line heights that plague amateur typography.

knowledgeCheck.question: What does a Red Eye icon on the lower-right corner of a text frame indicate in Affinity Publisher?
options: The text frame has red-eye removal active.
The text frame has Overset Text (overflowing text that cannot fit within the visible frame boundary).
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The red eye indicates overset text. You must enlarge the frame, thread the text to another frame, or reduce font size to reveal the hidden text.

knowledgeCheck.question: If your baseline grid is set to 14 pt, what should your paragraph leading or heading leading ideally be set to?
options: Multiples or exact divisions of the 14 pt grid (e.g. 14 pt, 28 pt, 42 pt) to prevent awkward skipping of grid rungs.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Using multiples of the baseline grid ensures larger headings occupy exactly 2 or 3 grid increments, allowing subsequent body text to resume without vertical disruption.

summaryPoints: Baseline grids create an unbroken vertical rhythm across columns and spreads.
Headline leading should always be configured as whole-number multiples of the grid spacing.
Multi-column text frames eliminate the need to manually align separate single-column boxes.
Text threading connects narrative flow dynamically across complex publication architectures.

slides.title: Baseline Grids, Flow Columns & Frame Margins
slides.subtitle: The Invisible Architecture of Editorial Rhythm
slides.contentMarkdown:
Look closely at any world-class newspaper, editorial magazine, or Swiss-designed book:

Notice how the lines of text in the left column align with millimeter precision to the lines of text in the right column.

In this lesson, you will master **Affinity Publisher's Baseline Grid Manager, multi-column text frames, and text threading**.

actionBox.label: The Swiss Secret
actionBox.text: Vertical rhythm is the heartbeat of typography. Lock your baselines, and your layouts instantly become professional.

slides.title: The Theory of the Baseline Grid
slides.subtitle: An Invisible Ladder for Letterforms
slides.contentMarkdown:
A **Baseline Grid** is a series of evenly spaced horizontal guides running down every page of your document:

- The spacing matches your primary **Body Copy Leading** (e.g. `14 pt`).
- When paragraphs are set to 'Align to Baseline Grid', the baseline of every letter automatically snaps to the nearest grid rung.
- Even when text wraps around an image or encounters a large headline, the subsequent body text immediately re-locks onto the grid.

slides.title: The Baseline Grid Manager & Text Frames
slides.subtitle: Precision Configuration
slides.contentMarkdown:
Access via `View > Baseline Grid Manager`:

- **Use Baseline Grid:** Master toggle to activate the system.
- **Grid Spacing:** Set to your leading (e.g. `14 pt` or `5 mm`).
- **Start Position:** Align to 'Top margin' or 'Top of page'.
- **Display Threshold:** Set to `50%` so grid lines remain visible at comfortable zoom levels.

**Frame Text Tool (T):** Context bar allows setting columns (`3`) and gutters (`5mm`) inside a single frame.

actionBox.label: Pro Shortcut
actionBox.text: Press T to activate Frame Text Tool. Drag to draw multi-column boxes.

slides.title: Step-by-Step: Setting Up 3-Column Threaded Spreads
slides.subtitle: Threading Editorial Copy Across Facing Pages
slides.contentMarkdown:
1. **Activate Baseline Grid:** Open `View > Baseline Grid Manager`. Check `[x] Use baseline grid`, set spacing to `14 pt`, and check `[x] Show baseline grid`.
2. **Draw Left Page Frame:** Select Frame Text Tool (`T`). Draw a frame across Page 2 margins. On Context Bar, set `Columns: 3` and `Gutter: 5mm`.
3. **Draw Right Page Frame:** Draw a matching 3-column frame across Page 3.
4. **Thread Text:** Click the small blue triangle at the lower-right of the Page 2 frame. Click inside the Page 3 frame to link them.
5. **Insert Filler Text:** Right-click inside Page 2 > `Insert Filler Text`. Notice copy flowing across all 6 columns!
6. **Lock Paragraphs:** In Paragraph Studio, check `[x] Align to baseline grid`. Notice lines across both pages lock into laser alignment.

visual.content: A red eye icon in the lower-right corner alerts you to Overset Text (hidden content).

slides.title: Typographic Traps & Headline Math
slides.subtitle: Preventing Staggered Text and Overflow
slides.contentMarkdown:
### 1. Breaking the Rhythm with Arbitrary Headlines
- **The Trap:** Setting a 24pt headline with 27pt leading on a 14pt grid. The body text below skips awkward fractions.
- **The Rule:** Always set headline leading to **multiples of the grid** (e.g. `28 pt` or `42 pt`).

### 2. Overset Text Blindness
- **The Trap:** Text overflows the frame and is silently omitted from the exported PDF.
- **The Fix:** Always inspect the **Preflight Studio** (`Window > Preflight`) before export. It catches all overset text errors instantly.

### 3. Multiple Unlinked Text Frames
- **The Fix:** Never draw 3 separate text frames for 3 columns. Use 1 frame with 3 columns in the Context Toolbar.

slides.title: Independent Challenge: Feature Article Spread
slides.subtitle: Put Vertical Rhythm into Practice
slides.contentMarkdown:
### Your Mission:
Construct a full feature magazine article layout on Pages 2 and 3:

1. Baseline grid locked to `14 pt`.
2. Page 2 has a bold 2-column headline with leading set to `42 pt` (3 × 14pt).
3. Body copy set to 10pt with 14pt leading, locked to baseline grid.
4. Thread text to Page 3 across 3 columns.
5. Align the bottom baseline of all columns to the bottom margin guide.

### Acceptance Criteria:
- Horizontal baseline alignment verified across both pages.
- Zero overset text warnings (Preflight panel green).
- Text flow threads continuously without break.

checkpoints: Threaded text flow across spread with zero overset
